approach: Add a read-only per-stage breakdown computed from existing records, with no new record type and no change to `Throughput::text`. A new `status/stages.rs` builds `StageBreakdown`. For each of the newest 5 landed jobs (`landed_jobs`, throughput.rs:472) it lists the stages in order: queue wait, reading, each planning round, producer, checks, verifier, landing, disk wait. Each stage is `{name, minutes: Option<f64>, reason: Option<String>, also: Vec<String>}`. Minutes come from record timestamps. Queue wait is the first reader `started_at` minus `Request.received_at`. Reading, producer and verifier are the summed wall time of that role's invocations. A planning round is the planner invocation named by `JobPlan.invocation_seq` plus the critic invocation named by `Critique.invocation_seq`. A job with no plan records gets one `planning` stage from its planner and critic invocations, or `not recorded` if it has none. Checks are the measured `CheckRun.duration` values. Landing runs from the last invocation end to the oldest landing record that names the job. Disk wait has no record, so it is always `not recorded`. The main reason is the first known item of: retries, tokens, turns and tool calls, model and effort. For checks it is the largest of test time, compile/lint time and build-slot wait. `throughput.rs` takes the OLDEST landing record instead of the newest, because docs/design/agent-and-build-slots.md:247-254 measured 4.3 to 11.0 minutes to the first record against 1220 to 2112 minutes to the newest. `display.rs` prints the breakdown after the throughput block in `athena status` and `athena status --snapshot`. A missing minute or reason prints `not recorded`. Revision: this answers the one finding. Criterion 3's demonstration command is now a plain command with the concrete absolute evidence path (derived from this plan's own working directory) and no angle brackets, redirection, variable or chaining; `git log` is a second, separate command.

decisions.choice: Put the breakdown in its own StageBreakdown (status/stages.rs) with its own StatusView and SnapshotView field. Leave Throughput and Throughput::text alone.
decisions.reason: Throughput::text is embedded in the throughput review (hestia.rs:2548) and asserted by `shown.contains(&throughput)` in crates/athena-cli/tests/status_snapshot.rs:116-119 and by many status.rs tests. A separate section cannot break them. The --json equality at status_snapshot.rs:94-96 compares only `throughput`, so a new sibling field is unaffected. Documented fields reused, each for what its name and comment say: Invocation.model, effort (an `Option<String>`, 'The effort level the agent ran at (`--effort`)'), tokens (Tokens), turns, commands_run (records.rs:755-770); Request.received_at (records.rs:437); JobPlan.invocation_seq 'The planner's invocation, as numbered in the job's `invocations/` directory' (records/plan.rs:102-103); Critique.invocation_seq 'The critic's invocation; none when Athena's own checks stopped the round before any critic call' (plan.rs:164-165); CheckRun.duration (records.rs:874); CheckRun.queued_s, the seconds the check waited in the build-slot queue (records.rs:902-906). queued_s is a wait before the check starts, so it ranks beside the check durations and is not added to the stage minutes.

rejected.option: Extend Throughput with per-job stage vectors and change its text()
rejected.why: Changes the text the throughput review stores and every test that matches its wording, and mixes a per-job view into a window median.

rejected.option: Add a new record type for stage timing
rejected.why: Out of scope. The timestamps already exist, and the records allow-list (check_record_file, AnyRecord) stays untouched.

decisions.choice: Landing record time is the oldest `created_at` among landing records that name the job as a JobLanding commit (`.min()`), not the newest. A new `pub(super) landing_record` returns that record so the landing stage can name its PR and merge method.
decisions.reason: `Landing.created_at` is documented 'When the landing was recorded' (athena-data/src/history.rs:224-225). The current code takes `.max()` (throughput.rs:389-403). One job is listed in many records: docs/design/agent-and-build-slots.md:247-254 measured job 20261104-054754-b4f5 at 4.3 min to the first record against 2112.0 min to the newest, and the five-job median at 4.6 min against 1337.0 min. `commits()` (gh/records.rs:128-143) lists every PR commit between the expected base and the head, which is why a later PR re-lists a job. With one record per job, min equals max, so existing tests keep their figures. That doc marks 'the first record is the real merge' as inferred, not checked (docs/design/agent-and-build-slots.md:257-261); criterion 3 on the real records is the check. Landing record shapes: (a) one JobLanding record naming the job: the oldest and only one. (b) Several records naming the job: the oldest wins. (c) A record whose commits are only DeclaredIntervention or RecordsOnly (history.rs:149-156): filtered out by `kind == JobLanding` (throughput.rs:396-399), so an intervention or records-only commit never moves a job's landing. (d) A blocked or retried landing: `intent()` writes only a LandingIntent and `landing()` writes the Landing after the merge (gh/records.rs:178-250), so a blocked PR leaves no Landing record and the retry's record is the oldest that names the job. (e) A catch-up record: same type, same filter; if it is the only record its time is used, a stated limit. (f) No record: landing is `not recorded`.

rejected.why: It gave the 1000-plus minute landing figures measured in docs/design/agent-and-build-slots.md:247-254; the criterion-3 range check on real records would fail.

rejected.option: Use the host commit's committed_at from history.json
rejected.why: Throughput::compute reads records only; history.json exists only in snapshot::status, and the independent range the criterion checks against must not be computed by the change.

decisions.choice: Landing stage minutes are None (printed `not recorded`) when no landing record names the job. When one does, minutes run from the last invocation end to max(outcome time, oldest record time), as landing_end does (throughput.rs:405-413) and as LandedJob.stages.landing_and_rebuild already holds (throughput.rs:491).
decisions.reason: The brief asks for durations measured from records, not a stand-in. landing_end falls back to the outcome time, which prints about 0.1 minutes. The existing Throughput medians keep that fallback unchanged, so no existing figure moves.

rejected.option: Print the outcome-time fallback as the landing time
rejected.why: It is the 0.1 minute figure criterion 3 calls wrong.

decisions.choice: The main reason is the first known item of a fixed order: retries, tokens, turns and tool calls, model and effort. The rest go in `also`. Tokens print as the sum of the known input, output, cache read and cache write values, with the split in the text. For checks the main reason is the largest of test time, compile/lint time and summed build-slot wait. A stage with no known item has reason None.
decisions.reason: Deterministic, uses only stored fields, needs no cutoff. A retry is more than one invocation of the role in the stage, or a planning round after the first. The split keeps cache reads from reading as new work. Compile/lint time is every check not named `test`, because CheckRun keeps no kind; throughput.rs:47-53 already treats the check named `test` as the test check. A single `checks::is_test_check` becomes that one rule, shared with `test_check_seconds`.

rejected.option: Pick the reason by a slowness threshold
rejected.why: Any threshold is a guess not measured here.

rejected.option: Use CheckSpec.kind (capability.rs:85) for compile/lint versus test
rejected.why: CheckRun records no kind, only a name.

decisions.choice: Disk wait is always a stage with minutes None and reason None, printed `not recorded`.
decisions.reason: No record holds a disk-hold duration (Invocation, Outcome and CheckRun have no such span), and adding a record type is out of scope.

rejected.option: Infer disk wait from the gap between outcomes

decisions.choice: Exits of the new breakdown computation, one per line. The reader of every None is `display::stage_lines`, which maps each None to the literal `not recorded`.
decisions.reason: (a) No landed job: `StageBreakdown::compute` returns None, serde skips the field, display prints nothing; the same condition as Throughput::compute. (b) A landed job with no invocation: `landed_jobs` drops it (throughput.rs:479, the `?` on the last invocation end). (c) A reader, producer or verifier invocation missing: that stage's minutes and reason are None. (d) No Request record: queue wait is None. (e) A planner or critic invocation seq not found: that round's minutes are None. (f) No JobPlan or Critique record at all: one stage named `planning` is built from the job's planner and critic invocations, or None when it has none. (g) No Verification or all checks `not run`: checks minutes and reason are None (the same `basis() != "not run"` test as check_minutes, throughput.rs:381). (h) No landing record: landing minutes None, reason 'no landing record names this job'. (i) A negative gap from clock skew is clamped with `.max(0.0)` as role_minutes does (throughput.rs:365-373). (j) Interrupt, hold, failure and error cannot happen: only Closed(Landed) jobs are listed and the function reads records and writes nothing. `athena status` writes nothing, so no hold, interrupt or error state is left behind.

decisions.choice: The printed landing line uses the words `landing time N minutes` and every stage line prints `minutes`, not `min`.
decisions.reason: D183 (docs/decisions.md:5321-5354) judges a real-records criterion by a measure phrase followed by a number and a whole-word unit of the range's family. The criterion's phrase is `landing time` (measure_phrase, records_criteria.rs:275-284, applied to criterion 3's text). The same wording lets Athena run criterion 3 on the producer's tree before the verifier. The criterion states no readable range after `expected range` (stated_range, records_criteria.rs:314-344, finds `from the landing...` and no number), so Athena records the run and does not judge it by range. A job with no landing record prints `landing time not recorded`, which has no figure and so is not judged.

rejected.option: Print `min` as the existing throughput text does
rejected.why: D183 reads only whole-word units, so the figure would not be judged.

decisions.choice: Answer to the finding on criterion 3: the demonstration command is `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot <job>/evidence`. It has no angle brackets, redirection, variable, backtick or chaining. The `git log` comparison is a second, separate command.
decisions.reason: The evidence directory is `evidence_dir(state, job)` = `state.job_dir(job).join("evidence")` (snapshot.rs:34-36), and `job_dir` is `root/jobs/ID` (state.rs:94-96). Planning writes its snapshot at `job_dir(id)/plan-N` (run/planning.rs:380), and this plan's working directory is `<job>/plan-1`. So the state root is `<state>` and the evidence path is the one above. Dispatch writes the snapshot with `snapshot::write(&self.git, head, &evidence)?` (run/mod.rs:1174-1175), and a failure to write or lock it fails the dispatch. The verifier is given the same path when the directory exists (verification.rs:199-200), and its brief tells it to run exactly `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot {path}` (briefs.rs:669). I could not list that directory (the read policy refuses paths outside plan-1), so the path is derived from code, not seen. If the verifier's brief names a different path, the verifier uses that one; the command is otherwise identical.

rejected.option: The placeholder `<job>/evidence` or `<committed evidence directory>` inside the command
rejected.why: The command check reads the angle brackets as a redirection; that is the finding. (The criterion's own text keeps `<committed evidence directory>`; snapshot_args at records_criteria.rs:246-271 skips it through its closing `>`, which is how Athena maps it to the real path for its own run, and the plan does not edit the criterion.)

rejected.option: The bare word `evidence` that records_criteria.rs:246-271 accepts
rejected.why: Athena rewrites that word to the real path only for its own run on the producer's tree (records_criteria.rs:680-697); a verifier running it would resolve `evidence` against its own copy, which has no such directory.

rejected.option: One chained command with `&&` for status and git log
rejected.why: The brief asks for git log as its own simple command, and a chain is judged one simple command at a time.

decisions.choice: No refusal or reading rule changes, so no refusal_corpus case is added.
decisions.reason: The reading for this job was already accepted. `check_records_measure` and its accepting case `records-measure-change-with-real-records-range-history-json` (refusal_corpus.rs:343-427 onward) are not touched. `is_test_check` moves an existing equality (`name == "test"`) and parses no input. The corpus mentions throughput.rs only as a deliverable path string (lines 379-414), not as code it calls.

rejected.why: The corpus tests reading and plan refusal rules, not the status printer.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in status/stages.rs build one landed job as in-memory records (request, reader, planner and critic invocations with JobPlan and Critique round records, producer, checks with queued_s, verifier, outcome, one landing record) and call StageBreakdown::compute. A second fixture has two planning rounds; a third has no plan records and falls back to one `planning` stage. The diff also shows the Stage struct fields `minutes`, `reason` and `also`.
demonstrations.observes: Stage names come out in order: queue wait, reading, planning round 1, producer, checks, verifier, landing, disk wait. The two-round job lists `planning round 1` then `planning round 2`. Each stage has Some minutes equal to the fixture's timestamp differences, and a reason where the fixture holds the data.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without stages.rs the StageBreakdown, JobStages and Stage types do not exist and the test module does not compile. Dropping a stage such as planning rounds or disk wait fails the assertion on stage names in `the_breakdown_lists_all_eight_stages_in_order`.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry `StageBreakdown::compute(&Records)`, added by step 4. The fixture is in-memory `Records` and `JobRecords` built by the test. The existing helpers `invocation` (status.rs:2073) and `timed_job` (status.rs:3022) are `pub(crate)` inside the `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) mod planning_cost_tests` (status.rs:2060-2061), so the sibling module reaches them as `crate::status::planning_cost_tests::{invocation, timed_job}`. `landing_of` (status.rs:3290) is private today; step 3 makes it `pub(crate)`. No double replaces any logic; the fixture is only records.

demonstrations.method: Display unit tests in crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs call `stage_lines` on hand-built StageBreakdown values: one fully recorded job, one with a None minutes and a None reason, and one with no landing record. `stage_lines` is the function `display::status` and `display::snapshot_status` call after the throughput print. As its own command, `cargo test -p athena-cli --test status_snapshot` (step 7) runs the real binary on a snapshot of the lifecycle fixture.
demonstrations.observes: A recorded stage prints its name, N.N minutes and `main:` with the reason. A missing minute prints `not recorded` and a missing reason prints `main: not recorded`; neither prints 0 or 0.0. The disk wait line prints `not recorded`. The landing line begins `landing time`.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the display change `stage_lines` does not exist and the CLI snapshot test finds no `disk wait` line. A version that printed 0.0 for a missing time fails the assertion that the line contains `not recorded` and not `0.0`.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry `display::stage_lines` (added by step 6), called from `display::status` (display.rs:1364-1366) and `display::snapshot_status` (display.rs:1245-1247), both of which exist today. The unit-test input is a StageBreakdown value built in the test, with no double. The CLI test uses the existing `landed()` repository fixture and `athena_in` (status_snapshot.rs:40-52, 58-66).

demonstrations.method: Run the command above on the real evidence snapshot Athena wrote at dispatch (run/mod.rs:1174-1175). Athena also runs it on the producer's tree before the verifier (D183). Then, as a separate simple command, run `git log --first-parent -n 30 --format=fuller` and compare each printed landed timestamp and `landing time` figure with the committer time of that job's host commit (its Athena-Job trailer names the job). If the verifier's copy has only one commit, read `history.json` in the same evidence directory with the Read tool; it holds the same committer times for the newest 200 first-parent commits (snapshot.rs:38-54, 98-110). The range comes from git history and history.json, which the change does not compute.
demonstrations.observes: For each of the newest 5 landed jobs there is a header line naming the job id and its landed timestamp, then the stage lines in order, ending with `landing time` and `disk wait`. The landed timestamp is within a few to tens of minutes of the host commit's committer time. The `landing time` figure is a few to tens of minutes, not 0.1 and not hundreds (the old newest-record rule gave 1220 to 2112 minutes on five sampled jobs, docs/design/agent-and-build-slots.md:247-254). A job with no landing record prints `landing time not recorded`. The `disk wait` line prints `not recorded`.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the change the output has no per-stage lines, so the check that each recent landed job lists its stages fails. Using the newest record instead of the oldest prints a landing time of hundreds of minutes or more beyond the host commit time. The 0.1-minute outcome fallback is no longer printed, because that case prints `not recorded`.
demonstrations.seam: The real binary through `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot` on the real evidence directory. Entry points `snapshot::status` (snapshot.rs:251) and `display::snapshot_status` (display.rs:1196) exist today; the stage output they print is added by steps 4 to 6. Guards: `snapshot::status` fails if the directory is missing (snapshot.rs:252-257) or has no history.json; dispatch cannot succeed without the snapshot (run/mod.rs:1175) and Athena ends the job early if it is unreadable (records_criteria.rs:508-517, 759-767). No fake or fixture is injected; the data is real records.

demonstrations.method: Run `cargo test -p athena-core` and, as its own command, `cargo test -p athena-cli`. New tests in status/stages.rs, status.rs, checks.rs, display.rs and status_snapshot.rs: (1) a planning round with one planner call and one critic call, about 40 minutes and 900000 tokens, has a main reason starting `tokens 900000`; a round-2 fixture (a second planner call after a revise) has a main reason starting `retry`. (2) A checks stage with test 20 min, clippy 5 min and queued_s 30 s names `test time`; clippy 20 min and test 2 min names `compile/lint time`; queued_s largest names `build-slot wait`. (3) A job whose producer invocation has pending tokens, turns None, no commands and an empty model has reason None, and its line prints `not recorded`. (4) Disk wait is None for every job and prints `not recorded`. (5) Two landing records naming one job, 6 and 400 minutes after the verifier, give landing time 6 minutes. (6) The status_snapshot.rs test runs the binary on the `landed()` fixture and asserts the `disk wait` line holds `not recorded` and a `landing time` line exists.
demonstrations.observes: Each assertion holds after the change; the tests fail at base because the new symbols do not exist.
demonstrations.fails_without: The new tests reference StageBreakdown, is_test_check and stage_lines, so without the change they do not compile. Behavior checks that also fail: `a_slow_planning_round_names_its_tokens_or_its_retry` fails if the reason were the model name only; `a_slow_check_names_build_versus_test_time` fails if every check reported test time; `a_second_landing_record_does_not_move_the_landing_time` fails with `max`; `a_missing_reason_prints_not_recorded` fails if None printed as 0 or an empty string.
demonstrations.seam: Production entries `StageBreakdown::compute` (step 4), `landed_jobs` via `landing_record_time` (throughput.rs:472, 391), `checks::is_test_check` (step 2) and `display::stage_lines` (step 6). Core fixtures are in-memory Records built by the test with the existing helpers named under criterion 1; the CLI fixture is the existing `landed()` repository in status_snapshot.rs. No double replaces the logic under test.
